column1: #   args     '-' for none, otherwise an argument list split on spaces
#   shape    an extended regular expression EVERY line of stdout must match,
#            with \t standing for a tab; '-' means stdout must be EMPTY
#   rc       the exit status the contract promises
# The names %JAIL% %VM% %HELD% %ABSENT% %BADNAME% are filled in by
# tests/conformance/run.subr from the world of the adapter under test; see its
# header. Nothing here may be destructive: these vectors run against a real
# node in tier 5. The mutating verbs appear only with a name their contract
# requires them to refuse before they touch anything.
# Field order comes from the '# contract:' line above each function in
# every adapter states the same one.
# An ABSOLUTE PATH is all the shared contract says (the '# contract:' line
# reads "-> path"). It used to read ^/.+/%JAIL%$ here, which is CBSD's layout
# -- ${jailsysdir}/<name> -- written into an oracle three adapters answer:
# a pseudo-cluster guest keeps its configuration in a dataset CHILD, at
# <mount>/<name>/sys, precisely so that it travels with the guest (D-84 item 3),
# and it failed this row the first time the suite was pointed at it (tier 5).
# The layout each platform actually promises is pinned per adapter, harder than
# a suffix match was: tests/tier5/t_conformance_real.sh asserts the exact
# ${jailsysdir}/<name> AND that rc.conf_<name> is in it, and
# adapter_guest_links for a JAIL is empty on every platform -- a jail's dataset
# is already mounted where CBSD looks. There is deliberately no %VM% row: what
# a VM needs is precisely the thing that differs between platforms, which is
# why this function exists at all, so a single expected shape for it would be
# a fiction. tests/tier4/t_adapter_parse.sh pins the real adapter's answer.
